label: conj:q-gl-fiber-functor
title: Fibre-functor mediation of the $q$-Langlands correspondence
html:
Conjecture. Fibre-functor mediation of the q-Langlands correspondence

Under the hypotheses of the q-Geometric Langlands conjecture, the Tannakian rigidity of the fibre functor \tau pins the correspondence: it forces \tau to determine the equivalence \mathbb{L}_q uniquely up to natural isomorphism:

  \mathbb{L}_q(\mathcal{M})(\mathcal{L}_q)
  \simeq
  \mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{Rep}(\check{G}_q)}
  \big(\tau(-),
  \mathrm{Hecke}_q(\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{L}_q)\big).

where \mathrm{Hecke}_q(\mathcal{M}, \mathcal{L}_q) is the tensor functor V_\lambda^{(q)} \mapsto \mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)}(\mathcal{M}) \otimes \mathcal{L}_q(V_\lambda^{(q)})_x^* encoding all Hecke eigenvalue data simultaneously. Evaluated at a single dominant weight \lambda, the right-hand side is the Hom-set into \mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)}(\mathcal{M}) \otimes \mathcal{L}_q(V_\lambda^{(q)})_x^* — the Hecke eigenvalue datum at that one \lambda; letting \lambda range over all dominant weights assembles these single-weight data into the equivalence above.

This uniqueness is the Tannakian rigidity of \tau (fibre-functor rigidity): any two equivalences compatible with the Hecke eigensheaf structure and the fibre functor are connected by a unique natural isomorphism.
